chunks: And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon on the last Friday of the month of Sha'ban, praising Allah and extolling Him.
Then he said: 'O people, a month has overshadowed you in which is a night 'better than a thousand months', the month of Ramadan.
Allah made its fasting obligatory, and He made the standing in prayer during one night of it, as voluntary, equivalent to the voluntary standing in prayer of seventy nights in the other months.

And He made for whoever voluntarily performs in it a characteristic from the characteristics of goodness and benevolence, like the reward of one who performed an obligatory duty from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.

And whoever performs in it an obligatory duty from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is like one who performed seventy obligatory duties from the obligations of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, in the other months.
And it is the month of patience, and indeed the reward for patience is Paradise.
And it is the month of sharing provisions, and it is a month in which Allah, Exalted and Glorious, increases the sustenance of the believer.
And whoever feeds a believer in it, for him is, because of that, with Allah, Exalted and Glorious, the freeing of a neck and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed.'
It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, not all of us are able to feed a fasting person in it.

He said: 'Indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is Generous; He gives this reward to whoever is not able except to give a mouthful of milk to a fasting person, or a sip of fresh water, or a few dates, which he cannot give more than that.
And whoever eases the burden on his slave in it, Allah will ease his reckoning.
And it is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance, and emancipation from the Fire.
And you have no need in it to be without four characteristics: two characteristics by which you please Allah, Exalted and Glorious, and two characteristics by which you have no need to be without.
As for the two by which you please Allah, Exalted and Glorious, they are the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
And as for the two by which you have no need to be without, they are that you ask Allah in it for your needs and Paradise, and you ask Allah for well-being and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.''

key_terms.قِيَامُ لَيْلَةٍ: Standing in prayer during one night

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and essential practices of Ramadan according to the Prophet's sermon?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this sermon (Khutbat Ramadan) serves as a foundational juristic and spiritual guide, emphasizing the multiplier effect of rewards where voluntary acts equal obligatory ones and obligatory acts equal seventy in other months. It highlights the month’s tripartite nature—mercy, forgiveness, and liberation from Hellfire—while stressing that even modest acts like a sip of water suffice for feeding a fasting person, reflecting the Shia emphasis on accessibility in worship. The hadith concludes by prescribing four essential practices: reaffirming faith, supplicating for needs and Paradise, seeking health, and seeking refuge from Hellfire, which aligns with the devotional practices of the Ahl al-Bayt.
